text:
anya: heads up — after the 10:30 canary we started seeing dashboard frameskip and slow chart paints on EU users. flamegraphs show main-thread parse/compile spikes and network waterfall is fine. looks correlated with the prefetch/kv-cache TTL tweak from yesterday. https://perf.internal/redwood/heatmap-17089 :thinking_face:

jordan: saw this on prod too. kvcache hit rate dropped ~40% after the rollout, CPU jumps when the chart tries to hydrate large sparklines. logs show repeated fetches for the same tile keys.

leo: the routing/quotas change adjusted client prefetch window and we lowered prefetch TTL to 5s for memory reasons. that was in the same rollout. might be the combo: smaller TTL -> more cold prefixes -> bundle parse thrash.

sam: if kvcache hit rate is low, prefix/KV misses will rehydrate large bundle pieces more often. that explains the parse spikes. we should either raise TTL back or make prefetch incremental.

anya: repro steps: load dashboard with ~20 rows, force a client nav, profiler shows repeated parsing of ~160KB chart chunk every 800ms for a subset of requests. snippet from console: ```
Network: GET /chunks/chart-v2-160kb.js 200 0ms (from service-worker)
Main: parse/compile chart-v2-160kb.js x3 per session
Cache: KV GET tile-prefix:abc -> MISS
```

maria: are any of those requests hitting routing fallback (regional -> global) so they go through different caches? that could make hit rates inconsistent. we should check edge routing logs.

leo: checking… the quota router recently started shard-splitting by tenant to avoid noisy neighbors. a handful of EU tenants got misclassified to the new shard and their cache affinity header changed. that could cause cross-region cache misses.

jordan: oof. can we patch policy to keep affinity for existing cookie users? quick fix: revert TTL to previous 60s and pin prefetch affinity header until we verify.

anya: agree. what's the minimum change to reduce user impact? rollback rollout? partial?

deploy-bot: canary deploy 2024-04-07T10:30Z id=canary-574 applied to 12% traffic. revert available: /revert canary-574

sam: revert TTL to 60s now, monitor kvcache hit rate. if hit rate recovers we can then safely revert shard-splitting config for the misclassified tenants.

leo: I'll do the TTL revert and add a server-side affinity header override for affected tenants. pushing PR now, tagging @anya for verification.

anya: thanks — after revert, run quick e2e on EU canary and post perf graphs. if main-thread parse goes down we can merge a proper fix: incremental prefetch + smaller chunking.

maria: I'll watch SLO alerts and cut a rollback if frame drops > 3x baseline for 10m.

jordan: follow-up items: 1) telemetry label about shard-split event, 2) add kvcache hit-rate dashboard with per-affinity dimension, 3) long-term: adaptive TTL heuristic per workload.

leo: PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/eng-platform/pulls/834 -- reverting client.prefetch.ttl and adding affinity override. running canary patch deploy.

anya: assigning leo as owner for hotfix. thanks everyone — keep messages here and paste perf snapshots. :thumbsup:
